start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:keep-commercial-events-once with store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_shop on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-shop-postgres-connection\"} and events [{\"event_id\": \"contract-shared-1\", \"event\": \"contract_shared\", \"subject_kind\": \"person\", \"subject_id\": \"person:example-buyer\", \"funnel_id\": \"sales\", \"stage\": \"shared\"}]."
no_lists_because: It names no list: the events are kept in the person's own store, in whatever form that store keeps things, and store says where and in which language.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the store is and how it is spoken to.
2. Say "Run workflow:keep-commercial-events-once" with store and the events to keep.
3. The first run makes the store's own objects once and proves them on the example attempts: every attempt must be kept, repeated or refused as the intent says, or the run stops and says which.
4. Every later run keeps the new events through those objects and reads each one back; a refused event comes back with the store's own words for why.

worked_examples.title: A contract shared, kept once
worked_examples.ask: Note that I shared the contract with the example buyer.

store.where: postgresql database example_shop on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The look step found the events kept in the table commercial_event with its keep function, made by an earlier run.
